Native and cross-platform app development

Compare native iOS and Android app development with a shared codebase around device features, user needs and the work your team will maintain.

Native iOS

Build in Swift when the app needs a close fit with Apple devices and platform conventions. Agree whether the first release supports iPhone, iPad or both, and test the features that depend on the operating system.

Native Android

Use Kotlin where the product needs Android-specific capabilities. Pick representative screen sizes and devices for testing. Include the permissions, navigation and compatibility cases that matter to your users.

Shared iOS and Android code

Cross-platform app development with Flutter or React Native can reduce duplicate work for apps with similar features on both platforms. Check early whether the app needs native modules, and plan separate store testing for both builds.

Connect accounts, data and devices

Plan the integration work as part of iOS and Android app development. Confirm which system owns each record and what the user should see when a connection fails.

Sign-in and roles

Give customers, employees and administrators the screens and actions they need. Define session expiry, password recovery and what happens when an account loses access.

Notifications and payments

For cross-platform app development, check how notification permissions and payment flows differ by device. Test cancelled, failed and successful payments, and show customers how to confirm an order or booking without repeating it.

APIs and offline sync

Our mobile app development services can connect existing systems or scope new endpoints for the required features. Document the records each connection reads or updates, and decide how to reconcile entries after time offline.

Explore automation and integrations

Define a first release you can test

Use mobile app development services to prove the most important workflow first. A short list of acceptance checks gives your team a way to say when that release is ready.

Agree what the first version must do

Describe the user, their starting point and the outcome they need. For a booking app, that might be finding a slot, confirming it and seeing the booking in their account. Decide which admin functions are needed to keep that journey running and which features can wait.

Set the device and access plan

For iOS and Android app development, decide which devices, operating system versions and account roles the first version needs to support. Use a small test group that reflects your audience. Identify a reviewer for accessibility and check which device permissions need explaining inside the app.

Plan how to review integration failures

Give testers a sample account and known states to try, such as an expired session, a rejected payment or a device that has lost its connection. For cross-platform app development, record which checks apply to both builds and which need a separate result on each platform.

When this support helps

Customer bookings and self-service

Cross-platform app development can suit a booking flow that works the same on iOS and Android. Agree how cancellations and reminders work and what happens if a slot is no longer available.

Field work with intermittent connectivity

Use mobile app development services to capture checklists, photos and job status from a phone. Show staff when entries are saved locally and when a supervisor can see them. Decide how to handle conflicting changes.

An app that needs another release

Start mobile app maintenance with a review of crash reports, third-party packages and store requirements. Reproduce problems on the affected devices and prioritise the fixes that unblock the next release.

How the work gets done

  1. 01

    Define the first release

    Choose the audience, primary workflow and supported devices. For mobile app development services, agree how users will sign in, what systems they need and which criteria will make the release ready.

  2. 02

    Prototype, build and test

    Review the main screens before implementation. During iOS and Android app development, test working builds early and check the mobile and backend flows together, including failed requests and recovery.

  3. 03

    Release and hand over

    Prepare store assets and change notes. Review what is ready to ship, who owns the store and build accounts, and which issues or updates fall under mobile app maintenance.

Release checks for mobile app development services

  • Test sign-in, account recovery and permissions with each user role.
  • Check key journeys on supported devices with slow or interrupted connections.
  • Review labels, focus order, text scaling and screen reader behaviour.
  • Confirm how failed payments, bookings or syncs are shown and retried.
  • Review store metadata, privacy disclosures, signing access and test accounts before submission.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can we launch on one platform first?

Yes. We can scope iOS and Android app development in phases. Tell us which devices your users have and which features they need. We’ll check whether decisions for the first app affect the second release.

When does a shared codebase make sense?

Cross-platform app development suits products whose screens and behaviour are largely shared. We compare development effort, native features, performance goals and the cost of maintaining both builds.

Can the app connect to our website or CRM?

Yes, where you have authorised API access. We define which system owns the records, what the app can update and how it handles missing data or delayed responses.

Can you take over an app that is already live?

We can review the code, dependencies, release accounts and open issues. That review gives us a basis for scoping bug fixes, upgrades and other mobile app maintenance.

What affects the cost and schedule?

Mobile app development services vary with the number of features, platforms, integrations, user roles and tests required. A clear first release and a named reviewer make it easier to estimate the build.

Who controls the source code and store accounts?

We agree code ownership, licence terms and account access when scoping mobile app development services. The handover can include the agreed source, a build guide and a record of the settings needed for future releases.
